paragraphs.source_en: The first four elements of the list, namely the body paintings, sticks, horned figures and bows appear throughout the whole area in the Tassili Plateau, in the Algerian Tadrart, in the Tadrart Acacus and also in the recently discovered area of the Aramat, North of the Acacus (Soleilhavoup 2007). Due to their presence in the majority of the sites, these elements are likely to represent the essential features of the Round Head culture which are common to all groups producing the paintings.

paragraphs.source_en: In contrast, bracelets, T-shaped objects, half-moons and the Great Gods, do not appear everywhere but they are limited to the Tassili Plateau. The most varied and numerous elements of the Round Head painted repertoire are therefore concentrated in the highest altitude of the region, precisely in the central-southern part of the Tassili Plateau. The surrounding mountains of the Algerian Tadrart and the Acacus present only those elements common for the whole area and do not seem to have their own particular motifs. The painted repertoire in these mountains is rather poor and it presents only eleven of the characteristic elements whereas the Tassili Plateau presents eighteen.

units.source_en: Why were certain elements represented only on the Tassili Plateau and not everywhere?
There may be at least three explanations:

paragraphs.source_en: - 1. The Tassili was occupied or frequented only by certain groups who used their own peculiar motifs which were not used by groups in the Acacus or in the Algerian Tadrart. - 2. The Tassili was frequented by all groups producing Round Head art but it was an area utilised for special occasions necessitating the use of these particular elements, reproduced in rock art. - 3. The difference in painted motifs may be caused by a chronological distinction between the Tassili and the lower mountains.

paragraphs.source_en: The characteristic motifs are not distributed equally throughout the Tassili Plateau but vary according to sites. Sefar, for example, includes all of the characteristic elements, whereas In Eleghi only displays two of them. If the quantity of the elements in a site indicates its value, it testifies to the unequal status of sites occupying the same Plateau.
